text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- The pre-registration of shares in the privatisation of EDP-Electricidade de Portugal starts today. Prices set by the cabinet last Thursday are considered low by the market and may prevent the state from gaining between 30 and 40 billion escudos.

- In 1994 and 1995 people depending on salaries were the group hit hardest by taxes. The Socialist Government defends a fairer distribution of wealth and aims via tax reform to tax more efficiently those outside the save-as-you-earn system and to increase the tax burden paid by the wealthiest.

- Public television station RTP is about to receive a loan that will allow savings of 700 million escudos in interest payments, as part of a campaign to tidy up its finances. It will receive 25 billion escudos from the state this year.

- Agriculture Minister Gomes da Silva said in an interview with the paper that areas of land dedicated to cereals production should decline as the sector is uncompetitive. Farmers should focus their efforts increasingly on other crops, he said.
- Tavares Moreira, chairman of agricultural bank Credito Agricola, said his bank was seeking business opportunities in Brazil in partnership with investment bank Banco Pactual.
- The third stage of privatisation of Portugal Telecom has been delayed to November from an expected sell-off in October, duer to "technical factors," a government official said.
